SBE order entry and private data
Last update: October 27, 2026
OKX plans to introduce Simple Binary Encoding (SBE) services for order entry and private order and fill updates. The services are expected to launch in the demo trading environment in early November 2026 and in the production environment in early December 2026 .
Existing REST and JSON WebSocket APIs will remain unaffected.
New SBE services
Service Production URL Demo trading URL XML schema Order entry wss://ws.okx.com/ws/v5/trade-sbe wss://wspap.okx.com/ws/v5/trade-sbe okx_sbe_trade_2_0.xml Private data wss://ws.okx.com/ws/v5/private-sbe wss://wspap.okx.com/ws/v5/private-sbe okx_sbe_private_1_1.xml
The login method is the same as that of the existing SBE Market Data service . Authentication is completed during the WebSocket HTTP Upgrade request by providing the API key and signature in the request headers.
JSON control messages use text frames with opcode 1 , while SBE messages use binary frames with opcode 2 .
Compared with the JSON services, the fields in SBE messages are streamlined. Refer to the XML schemas for the complete message layouts and field definitions.
XML schema updates
The XML schemas have been updated ahead of launch. Please use the latest versions above to generate your encoders and decoders.
Order entry: okx_sbe_trade_2_0.xml
Schema id changes from 1 to 2 ; version remains 0 , and semanticVersion changes to 2.0.0 . The message layouts change; regenerate your encoders and decoders using this schema. Single and batch place-order requests add optional rpiPxRound (RPI price rounding) and reduceOnly fields. Single and batch amend-order requests add optional rpiPxRound . In single and batch place/amend requests, expTime is renamed to expTimeUs . In all place/amend/cancel responses, ts is renamed to tsUs . These fields continue to use microseconds. Single and batch place-order responses remove instIdCode ; subsequent fixed fields shift forward and their field IDs change. Single place/amend/cancel responses add the variable-length UTF-8 error message msg . Batch place/amend/cancel responses rename the data group to results , with entries in request order (up to 20). They add the sMsgDetails group containing per-order error messages ( sMsg ), linked to results by the zero-based resultIndex , and a batch-level msg . Both msg and sMsg use varString16 , a variable-length UTF-8 string with a uint16 length prefix.
Private data: okx_sbe_private_1_1.xml
Schema id remains 1 ; version changes from 0 to 1 , and semanticVersion changes to 1.1.0 . The orders message adds optional reduceOnly ( booleanEnum : FALSE=0 , TRUE=1 ) and avgPxMantissa (average executed price mantissa, using pxExponent ). Both fields have sinceVersion="1" . In orders , fillTime , uTime , and cTime are renamed to fillTimeUs , uTimeUs , and cTimeUs . In fills , ts is renamed to tsUs . Their units remain microseconds, and the renamed fields retain their field IDs and types.
SBE order entry
The order entry service will support the following operations:
Place order and place multiple orders Amend order and amend multiple orders Cancel order and cancel multiple orders
Batch operations will support up to 20 orders. SBE order entry will support CASH and CROSS trading modes. Clients that require another trading mode should continue to use the JSON WebSocket trading API.
SBE private data
The private data service will support the following channels:
orders : Publishes an update when an order is created or its state changes. fills : Publishes order-book fill events and is available to VIP4 and above users.
Neither channel will publish an initial snapshot. Subscription requests and responses will remain in JSON format, while channel data will be encoded in SBE. The orders channel will support filtering by instType ; instIdCode is not required. For the fills channel, instIdCode is also not required.

Signal Clone — New API endpoint
Last update: May 14, 2026
OKX is adding API support for the Signal Clone (Order Sharing) feature. API traders can now generate a universal sharing link programmatically by passing an order ID. The link encodes the order parameters (instrument, side, leverage, price, TP/SL, etc.) server-side. Recipients who open the link will have those parameters prefilled in the OKX App trading panel.
This feature is scoped to USDT-margined perpetual contracts. Signal Clone must be enabled for the account.
Create signal link
Create signal link
A new endpoint POST /api/v5/copytrade/create-sgl-link is added. Pass orderId and instId in the request body. The order must belong to the requesting account. Only USDT-margined perpetual contracts ( instId ending in -USDT-SWAP ) are supported. Other instrument types will return an error. Returns a shortLink — a universal OKX App link that can be shared with others to prefill the trading panel with the order parameters. Rate limit: 10 requests per second per user.
Request example
POST /api/v5/copytrade/create-sgl-link
body { "orderId" : "3556007031710728192" , "instId" : "ADA-USDT-SWAP" }
Request parameters
Parameter Type Required Description orderId String Yes Order ID. Must belong to the requesting account. instId String Yes Instrument ID, e.g. BTC-USDT-SWAP . Only USDT-margined perpetuals are supported.
Response example
{ "code" : "0" , "data" : [ { "shortLink" : "https://www.okx.com/ul/1xJ7nV" } ], "msg" : "" }
Response parameters
Parameter Type Description shortLink String Universal sharing link. Recipients can open this link in the OKX App to have the order parameters prefilled in the trading panel.

https://www.okx.com/docs-v5/log_en#upcom.title: WebSocket port 8443 discontinuation
https://www.okx.com/docs-v5/log_en#upcom.content:
WebSocket port 8443 discontinuation
Last update: October 22, 2026
To support a network infrastructure upgrade, OKX will stop accepting WebSocket connections on port 8443, including Colo connections:
Public internet: October 31, 2026 Colo: November 16, 2026
Port 443 already works on all affected domains, including Colo, and both ports remain available until these dates.
Breaking change
After these dates, connections to port 8443 will fail. Remove :8443 from your WebSocket URLs. Only the port changes; the host and path stay the same. wss:// uses port 443 by default, and :443 also works. This applies to every path, including /ws/v5/public , /ws/v5/private , /ws/v5/business and, on the Global site, /ws/v5/public-sbe .
Public internet, from October 31, 2026 Production Before: wss://ws.okx.com:8443/ws/v5/public After: wss://ws.okx.com/ws/v5/public Demo trading Before: wss://wspap.okx.com:8443/ws/v5/public After: wss://wspap.okx.com/ws/v5/public Colo, from November 16, 2026 All Colo WebSocket connections on port 8443.
REST API is not affected.
Add error codes
Until these dates, connections on port 8443 receive a notification (event = notice ) with the following code once the handshake succeeds. The connection stays open.
Error code Error message 64010 WebSocket port 8443 will be retired soon. Please migrate to port 443.
